name: Sander Janca-Jensen
profile: Danish serial entrepreneur who co-founded card-payments company Flatpay (launched in Copenhagen in 2022) with Rasmus Busk, Peter Lüth and Rasmus Hellmund Carlsen. Flatpay sells simple flat-fee payment terminals to small merchants via field sales; a €145M round made it a unicorn (€1.5B). Before Flatpay he spent years at home-security firm Verisure.
interesting_fact: Flatpay was described as the fastest Danish company ever to reach unicorn status; he says the company prides itself on saying 'no' a lot internally.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Rasmus Busk come from field sales at security company Verisure, where they scaled a sales team of 400 people; he also tracks his routine closely ('If you don't measure stuff, you can't manage stuff'), lifting weights three times a week.

public_contacts.value: christian.gronning@flatpay.dk (Christian Grønning, Global Head of Communications)

notes: Measure/quote facts from Tech.eu profile (Jan 2026; URL slug mismatched but page title is 'The Danish fintech boss who says no a lot'). Best route is Flatpay's comms head. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane; contacts limited to Flatpay press release.

name: Carl Pei
profile: Beijing-born, Sweden-raised entrepreneur (b. 1989) who co-founded OnePlus with Pete Lau in 2013 and ran its global brand until 2020. In 2021 he founded London-based Nothing, backed by Tony Fadell, Casey Neistat and Steve Huffman among others; it makes the Nothing Phone and Ear lines plus lower-priced CMF sub-brand and is valued at over $1B.
interesting_fact: The OnePlus One sold close to a million units in 2014 against an initial target of 50,000.
deep_cut_fact: His first industry job came from a fan website he built about Chinese phone maker Meizu, which caught the attention of Meizu's Hong Kong branch; he then dropped out of the Stockholm School of Economics (2011) to work in China's smartphone industry, after a ~3-month Nokia internship in 2010.
notes: Very public and active on X; no published press email found on nothing.tech (search budget exhausted before finding press contact).

name: George Candea
current_role: Professor of Computer Science, EPFL (head of Dependable Systems Lab); co-founder of Cyberhaven
profile: Computer scientist (MIT BS/MEng, Stanford PhD 2005) who co-founded big-data firm Aster Data (2005, acquired by Teradata) and, in 2016, data-security company Cyberhaven with four of his EPFL PhD students. He served as Cyberhaven's CEO and later Chief Scientist and now focuses on his EPFL lab.
interesting_fact: ACM Fellow; recipient of the 2024 Mark Weiser Award, the inaugural EuroSys Jochen Liedtke Young Researcher Award (2014) and MIT TR35 (2005).
deep_cut_fact: Before Aster Data he held positions at Oracle, Microsoft Research and IBM Research; at EPFL he teaches 'The Software Enterprise: From Ideas to Products' and his lab page includes his own essay on what makes Switzerland special.
notes: Academic; most reachable of the Cyberhaven founders via his published EPFL email. Cyberhaven CEO since 2021 is Howard Ting.
